components.cost_effect: Residual generation, graph membership certification and inner solve work are separately charged; their cost is unspecified by this abstract outer Algorithm.
components.goal: Replace an inaccessible distance to the exact resolvent by a certifiable regularized inclusion residual.
components.key_estimate: Source Proposition 3: ||u-P_k(z^k)|| <= c_k dist(0,S_k(u)). For w in S_k(u), u=P_k(z^k+c_k w), so nonexpansiveness gives ||u-P_k(z^k)|| <= c_k||w||; taking the infimum proves the estimate. This is the complete source argument in paraphrase, not a new local transfer claim.
components.name: Residual stopping surrogate
components.operation: For the current z^k and c_k define S_k(u)=T(u)+c_k^(-1)(u-z^k). Require dist(0,S_k(u)) <= epsilon_k/c_k. A certified element w in S_k(u) with ||w|| <= epsilon_k/c_k suffices.
components.requires: A valid residual bound or a valid graph-element certificate; plain evaluations of an unrelated Oracle do not supply this automatically.
transfer_checks: Reestablish the residual-to-resolvent inequality if the geometry, regularization or Oracle feedback changes.
Verify summability of the resulting absolute errors; a merely vanishing residual tolerance is insufficient.

limitations.statement: The approximate-resolvent interface does not specify a primitive-Oracle implementation; its inner solve and certification costs can depend on tolerances and the problem.
The linked Theorem gives no finite outer iteration complexity or accuracy-based stopping schedule, and supplies weak convergence rather than general strong convergence.

performance_links.scope_note: Only the complete criterion (A) Theorem applies: positive lower parameter bound and boundedness or zero existence yield asymptotic weak convergence and vanishing residuals.

variants.cost: Each outer iteration makes one abstract approximate-resolvent request and one state replacement. After N steps this interface makes N such requests. Inner iterations, graph/gradient/value evaluations, linear solves and residual-certificate acquisition or validation must be charged separately according to the implementation; no tolerance-dependent inner cost is given here. The weak limit is not a finite computational output.

variants.name: Criterion (A) absolute-error iteration
variants.output: The source analyzes the full sequence {z^k} and its weak limit when the linked conditions hold. Under the explicitly selected finite-budget convention, return the last computed z^N; no finite-N solution accuracy is certified. An inexact iterate need not itself be a zero or, under criterion (A) alone, even belong to D(T).
public_inputs: A representation of a maximal monotone T on a real Hilbert space H and an approximate-resolvent routine with the stated error contract.
Initial point z^0 in H; positive parameters c_k and nonnegative tolerances epsilon_k with summable total error.

For the linked convergence guarantee, a positive lower bound on c_k and either existence of a zero or boundedness of the resulting sequence are required; a zero itself need not be supplied to the routine.
An optional finite outer budget N is a selected reporting convention, not an accuracy-dependent stopping schedule supplied by the paper.
variants.query_and_update: At outer step k request u=ApproxResolvent_T(z^k,c_k,epsilon_k), set z^(k+1)=u, then increment k. Equivalently, an inner solver may produce u satisfying dist(0,T(u)+c_k^(-1)(u-z^k)) <= epsilon_k/c_k, which implies the required absolute resolvent error by source Proposition 3. A sufficient implementable certificate is a supplied graph element v in T(u) with ||v+c_k^(-1)(u-z^k)|| <= epsilon_k/c_k; obtaining or verifying v is part of the inner implementation, not an assumed free step.
variants.requirements: T is maximal monotone; the approximate-resolvent interface accepts (z,c,epsilon) and returns u in H satisfying ||u-(I+cT)^(-1)(z)|| <= epsilon. Such an interface is an explicit computational capability, not a free consequence of graph access to T. For the linked Theorem impose inf_k c_k>0 and nonempty zero set or bounded generated sequence.
variants.state_and_initialization: Set k=0 and choose any z^0 in H. Maintain the current point and parameter/tolerance sequences. No zero or projection onto the zero set is needed for initialization.
variants.tuning_and_stopping: Use c_k>0 and epsilon_k>=0 with sum epsilon_k<infinity; the convergence link further requires inf_k c_k>0. Theorem 1 imposes no nondecreasing-c_k requirement. Criterion (A') is an inner stopping test when its residual bound can actually be certified. Run indefinitely for the asymptotic result, or stop after a user-specified N outer steps; the source supplies no finite outer accuracy certificate for this variant.

title: Inexact proximal point iteration with summable absolute errors
use_when: Implement the outer proximal point iteration when an approximate-resolvent interface or a certified residual inner solve is available.
